Its standalone suite and the 240 discovery samples were outside this run.General regular-completion proofWrite  $m=|E(G)|$ . Every old outsider already has degree  $r$ , so the selected deficits exhaust the deficits on each side:
$$D_A=r|A|-m,\qquad D_B=r|B|-m.$$
Consequently both integrality conditions reduce to  $p\equiv D_A\equiv D_B\pmod r$ . A uniform legal choice is  $p=p_0+2r$ , with  $p_0$  the least nonnegative residue. Both opposite-side supplies are then at least  $2(r-1)\ge r$ , enough for every old deficit and every new endpoint deficit  $r-1$ . This includes  $r=2$ .For a prescribed admissible  $p$ , take one side with deficits  $d_i$  and  $u$  new opposite-colour vertices. The necessary simple-edge capacity is  $d_i\le u$ . It is sufficient because  $\sum_i d_i=ru$ : give successive rows consecutive strings of  $d_i$  positions in  $0,\ldots,ru-1$ , reduced modulo  $u$ . No row repeats a neighbour, and each column occurs exactly  $r$  times. If  $u=0$ , every deficit on that side is zero. Applying the construction on both sides gives the required simple  $r$ -regular graph.For an outsider  $z$ , coverage depends exactly on whether it has two selected neighbours or has a selected neighbour incident to a selected edge. After deleting any old selected vertex  $v$ , every old witness retains its old selected neighbourhood, and each of those neighbours retains its old selected adjacencies. This includes a failure witnessed by  $v$  itself. Every new outsider is initially covered by its  $r$  selected neighbours. Deleting a new selected endpoint leaves it with just its mate as a selected neighbour, and the mate has no remaining selected neighbour. Thus every single deletion fails. Formation is upward closed, proving inclusion-minimality for arbitrary old selected-component structure.Old cap, fixed witness and cyclic familyBoth old caps are 31. Each of the eight  $P_6$  blocks contributes at most four vertices, since each of two disjoint consecutive triples contributes at most two. At total size 32 every block is full. Its six possible four-sets, in positions  $0,\ldots,5$ , are 0134, 0135, 0145, 0235, 0245, 1245. Replacing any pattern containing  $a$  by  $A=0235$ , and retaining  $B=1245$  otherwise, introduces no interface vertex and does not increase the internal degree of any retained interface vertex. Simultaneous normalization therefore preserves dissociation. A chain edge forbids  $A_jB_{j+1}$ , since  $b_{j+1}$  in state  $B$  is already paired with  $i_{j+1}$ . An  $A$  root forces its whole group to  $A$ , giving its terminal  $a$  two distinct retained neighbours. Both roots must then be  $B$ , and the root bridge joins two already paired  $b$ 's. This proves the cap with the port removed. Taking  $A$  in the first group and  $B$  in the second, then omitting  $a_3$ , attains 31 and omits port 30. The same set attains the cap with the port present.The fixed 38-set is an actual witness. Reconstructing the eight paths, the special edges and the 16 incidence rows from the note gives exactly the fixture's 102 edges. Each colour has old deficit 20. With  $p=2$ , the construction adds eight outsiders of each colour and fills every deficit. The 36 selected vertices induce eight  $P_3$ 's, eight isolates and two edges. Directly restricting the coordinate edge list to the displayed  $D$  gives the following 16 edges:
$$\begin{gathered}
(1,2),(4,5),(7,8),(15,16),(18,19),(22,23),(24,25),(29,53),\\
(30,31),(33,60),(35,62),(36,46),(38,39),(43,44),(48,54),(51,66).
\end{gathered}$$
The remaining six vertices are isolates  $10,13,27,41,58,63$ . Thus all 38 vertices have induced degree at most one, and  $6\notin D$ .Switching preserves the required data for every  $k$ . The map  $48j+t\mapsto68j+t$  identifies the switched old graph with the induced graph on the old vertices of the completion. Each replacement edge  $30_j6_{j+1}$  joins opposite-colour outsiders. For  $k=1$  it restores the original edge. For  $k=2$  the two cross-copy edges have distinct endpoint pairs. All old deletion witnesses survive switching, as do the new matching-endpoint witnesses. In the old core the failures after deleting  $x_j,c_j,y_j,i_j$  occur respectively at  $a_j,a_j,b_j,i_j$ .Any old dissociation set restricts to at most 31 vertices per deleted-port copy. The 31-set omits port 30, so its copywise union attains  $31k$ . The completed 38-set omits the other port, 6, so its copywise union likewise gains no induced edge. This gives
$$|S_k|-\beta_2(G_k)=32k-31k=k,\qquad
|T_k|-\beta_2(K_k)\le36k-38k=-2k.$$
Connectivity holds for all  $k$ . Each deleted-port old piece is connected through its root bridge. In the completion every new outsider touches the old core and every new matching endpoint attaches through such an outsider. The cyclic links therefore connect the completed graph. If deleting a vertex  $v$  of colour  $A$  leaves components  $C$ , the number of edges from  $v$  to each  $C$  is
$$t_C=r\bigl(|C\cap B|-|C\cap A|\bigr)>0.$$
These positive multiples of  $r$  sum to  $r$ , so there is only one component. This proves two-connectivity. For every  $k\ge2$ , deleting vertices 6 and 30 in one copy removes all its links to the other copies, separating its 66 remaining vertices from them. Hence  $\kappa(K_k)=2$  throughout the claimed range.
